search_coverage.summary: The supplied Controller packet reports sufficient coverage: 49 completed query events, 99 verified reads, 82 canonical decision-grade Evidence Cards, and a completed 19-paper active continuation subset with no declared gaps. The closest priors collectively cover simple Hunt–Crossley contact, finite-area and velocity-dependent contact control, deformable-contact geometry and friction, six-dimensional admittance, viscoelastic history, identifiability limits, and learned uncertainty. They establish that the technical ingredients and experimental instrumentation are known, but none resolves the combined scientific problem: an operating-condition map of the separate and combined incremental value of contact-information components for optimal impedance decisions and held-out outcomes, together with decision-equivalence, observability, reproducibility, and minimal-sufficiency tests. Problem novelty and scientific-delta novelty therefore remain; the randomized repeated-measures phantom/ex-vivo route itself is known instrumentation rather than the source of novelty.

novelty_assessment.residual_unresolved_delta: The unresolved scientific delta is not whether richer contact models can be constructed or used, but under which practical soft-scanning regimes each added information component—alone and in combinations—causally changes the selected optimal impedance and improves prespecified held-out closed-loop and independent scanning-quality outcomes, and what observable, reproducible, decision-equivalent minimal representation suffices for each improvement. No supplied prior resolves this component-by-condition-by-outcome minimality map under matched resources and nested ablations. The experimental route uses known models, sensing, optimization, phantom testing, and bounded ex-vivo confirmation, so technical-route novelty is limited; novelty resides in the falsifiable comparative problem and scientific decision-value map.
